supported.quote: The deployment renamed the metrics port from `metrics` to `http-metrics` in deploy/values-production.yaml, but deploy/scrape.yaml at that revision still picks the endpoint to scrape by the name `metrics`.
The ServiceMonitor selects by port name, and a name that matches no port does not raise an error to the operator. It just gives an empty target list, so Prometheus had nothing to scrape.

A planned renaming of the shop's network ports to a platform-wide naming rule also renamed the port the monitoring system collects the shop's measurements from, and the monitoring setup, which finds that port by its name, was not changed to match, so it had nothing to collect.
Until a deploy carries a matching scrape port name, io-shop's metrics stay uncollected
Shoppers saw nothing wrong, but the shop's metrics stopped arriving
Nobody using the shop was seen to have anything go wrong. What was seen instead: the shop's metrics stopped arriving, and the series went absent rather than crossing a threshold.

The metrics stopped because Prometheus had no target to scrape. At the revision that was running, the ServiceMonitor picks the endpoint by the port name `metrics` (S1), and no port at that revision has that name: the metrics port is named `http-metrics` (S2). The scrape config itself says that a name matching no port gives an empty target list, not an error.

No port was named `metrics` any more because the deploy of revision c3c36da at {P2.1} renamed every port to the `<protocol>[-<purpose>]` convention, including the metrics port, from `metrics` to `http-metrics` (D1).
As of {T13.1}, all replicas were running that revision.
The earlier deploy of revision 2c8f731: metrics were still collected with it in place, up to the minute before the onset.
The rename broke scraping because the change edited only deploy/values-production.yaml and left the scrape config still selecting the port by its old name.

No check was seen that the port name the ServiceMonitor selects agrees with the metrics port name in values-production.yaml. The scrape config at the revision that ran says that nothing checks this, so a change to only one of the two files could ship.

When the ServiceMonitor selects a port name that matches no port, the operator does not raise an error; it gives an empty target list. No alert on an empty scrape target list was seen, so the gap was found only by the MetricsAbsent rule once samples had been missing for its window.
The MetricsAbsent alert on io-shop paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
